 Kyle Shanahan identifies 49ers' main challenges for Week 9 matchup vs. Raiders 
 Ahead of the 49ers Week 9 matchup against the Raiders, coach Kyle Shanahan sat down with Matt Maiocco to talk about the challenges in facing them. 
 By Dylan Grausz • 
 Published November 6, 2026 • 
 Updated on November 6, 2026 at 9:24 pm 
 BOOKMARKER 
 Share 
 NBC Universal, Inc. 
 Kyle Shanahan, Christian McCaffrey, Nick Bosa and Fred Warner speak to reporters after San Francisco 49ers practice on Wednesday in Santa Clara. 
 Programming note: Matt Maiocco's interview with Kyle Shanahan on "49ers Game Plan" airs at 9 p.m. Friday on NBC Sports Bay Area .
 The 49ers take on the Las Vegas Raiders at home this week -- the third time in the Kyle Shanahan era the two teams will face off in the regular season.
 San Francisco is coming off a bye week, and while injuries still plague the team , multiple key players are expected back, including wide receiver Demarcus Robinson and edge rusher Nick Bosa . Their returns certainly will give the 49ers a much-needed boost, but that will not make the game any easier.

 The Raiders are 4-4 and look much improved from last season, shining in a variety of ways. Shanahan sat down with NBC Sports Bay Area's Matt Maiocco on "49ers Game Plan" and identified the key challenges that come with facing Las Vegas.
 “They’ve been real impressive with how they’re moving the ball, how many points they’ve put up, and they’ve been protecting it, too,” Shanahan told Maiocco. “They’ve struggled in the run game. We’ve got to make sure they don’t get that going. Anytime you struggle in the run game, it’s tough to put points up and to not have turnovers. But to me, the reason they’ve done it is because they’ve been so good on third down.
 “Kirk Cousins is playing at a very high level. He’s protecting the ball. I think they’re top 10 in turnovers, I know they’re top 10 in scoring points. Another top 10 on third down. Another top 10 in throwing the ball. So they’re a pretty explosive offense in that way, and they can get rolling even when they’ve been down a couple scores, three scores. 
 "I think it was 28-7 maybe vs. the Rams. They got it back to an eight-point game really fast. And [Cousins] does that, he distributes the ball and everything. But the guy who makes it go is [tight end] Brock Bowers. He is really impressive. Just getting to watch him this week -- I mean, I’ve seen him coming out of college, I’ve seen him a little bit over last year. But he’s definitely up there as one of the best, and he’s a tough guy to stop.”

 Cousins is having a resurgent season after an up-and-down two-season stint with the Atlanta Falcons. Through eight games, he has registered 2,124 passing yards, 19 touchdowns and only five interceptions while putting up a 101.4 passer rating. His rating is the highest he has posted since 2023.
 The 49ers need to play their best brand of football in order to win and keep a stronghold on the NFC West lead. After re-acquiring former first round pick DeForest Buckner in a trade with the Indianapolis Colts, San Francisco hopes that move is the key to a dominant second half of the season.
 A strong performance against the Raiders will set the team up nicely for a tough three-game stretch that includes games against the Dallas Cowboys, Minnesota Vikings and Seattle Seahawks.
 The 49ers are 6-1 and have big Super Bowl aspirations. If they continue to play at a high level the rest of the way and improve to 7-1 this week, expect them to be right in the mix to play at SoFi Stadium on Valentine's Day.
